documents.how_used: This is the primary document for 55 Pa. Code Ch. 2800 (ALR). It lists what the applicant must send to the BHSL headquarters office before the initial inspection is scheduled. Items 2(b), 3-6, 8, 9(b)-(g) and 10 are the policy and plan content used below. Application and non-policy items 1, 2 (clearances), 7, 9(a), 11-18 are excluded.

notes: Each checklist is submitted to the BHSL headquarters office before the initial inspection of a new facility, or of a sale or change of legal entity, is scheduled. The checklist says BHSL may request additional materials, or the materials in a different order than listed. The reviewer therefore expects the packet to follow the checklist's own numbering (1-18, with lettered sub-items), with each policy labelled by item number and regulation cite (e.g., '8(a) Reportable Incidents and Conditions Policy – § 2800.16(b)'). The ALR (Ch. 2800) and PCH (Ch. 2600) checklists are separate; a facility licensed as an ALR submits the ALR version and a PCH submits the PCH version. 'doc': 0 is the ALR checklist and 'doc': 1 is the PCH checklist. Items I left out of required_items as application or evidence paperwork, not policy content: 1 (administrator credentials), 2 (the criminal history clearances themselves), 7 (floor plans, elevator certificate, SCU/SDCU site evidence), 9(a) (written SCU/SDCU request), and 11-18. Item 1 (administrator qualifications) is also omitted from required_items, and it is the only omitted item that is partly staffing content. Item 10 is a list of 'forms' (contract, rights poster, fire drill record, assessment and support plan forms, MAR). I kept those as operating documents, not application forms. Drop them if you want strictly written policies. Special Care Unit / Secured Dementia Care Unit items and swimming pool, firearms and smoking policies apply only if applicable. The checklist for the Certificate of Compliance application (hs633-checklist.pdf) covers non-policy paperwork such as fees, occupancy permit and civil rights form. I did not use it. Those fees are not stated consistently across sources (for example, per-bed amounts), so check the current fee schedule. The Ch. 2800 and Ch. 2600 regulation sections cited in brackets are the authority for the content of each policy. I could not open the pacodeandbulletin.gov pages, so each policy's required contents come from the regulation text, which I did not read.
